# Metaprompt

## Git

### Allowed and encouraged

- Create new commits freely and often for atomic, well-scoped units of work.
  - Do not ask first.
  - Ensure applicable tests run and pass before each commit.
  - Every git operation is authorized by default and needs no per-use permission.
    - This includes rebase, pull, merge, reset, checkout, cherry-pick, force-push, and branch deletion.

commands.name: agent-token-usage
commands.description: Report per-agent token usage (main loop plus every subagent) for a Claude Code session as a table, where each row counts only that agent's own turns. Use when asked how many tokens were spent, for a token breakdown by subagent, or to audit a run's token cost. (user)

commands.name: analyze-position
commands.description: Walk through a structured analysis of a given chess position using CEE. Dispatches the full multi-axis analysis by default, or a single analyst axis (character, opening-book, endgame, criticality, stm-attack, stm-defense) when the first token names one. The full analysis creates its game through CEE's stable-tree build from a FEN, or from a saved game state with --game-state (loaded as-is, never regenerated). Use when the user asks to analyze a position, explain a move, walk through a blunder, analyze one axis of a position, or invokes /analyze-position. (user)

commands.name: build-status
commands.description: One-shot report of the current or last build.sh / quick_build.sh run for the current CEE workspace. Reports whether a build is running, succeeded, failed, was killed, or has never run. Use when the user asks about the state of the current build, whether it finished, failed, or is still going. (user)

commands.name: ceac-processor-script
commands.description: Create or update a utils/<name>/ script set (request generator + wrapper + README + pyproject) for driving a given CEAC websocket endpoint through the ceac-processor client. Use when asked to scaffold, add, or conform a batch-processing integration for a CEAC endpoint (e.g. /v1/evaluate-game, /v1/run-search, /v1/advanced-stats), mirroring the evaluate_games reference integration. (user)

commands.name: ceac-sandbox
commands.description: End-to-end test the current branch against the CEAC sandbox environment: reserve the sandbox, deploy the branch build, fire a branch-relevant request corpus, report failures, and always release the sandbox afterward. (user)

commands.name: create-or-update-pr
commands.description: Create a new GitHub PR for the current branch, or update the description of an existing one. Inspects the current branch's commits and diff, picks up to 2 relevant reviewers, and runs /check-cicd after. With `--rebase`, first brings the branch up to date by rebasing it onto the refreshed default base branch. With `--add-to-merge-queue`, also waits for the merge queue to pick up the PR and runs /check-cicd a second time on the merge queue CI. (user)

commands.name: cross-system-fanout
commands.description: Settle a cross-system implementation architecture with the user — first agreeing the ARCHITECTURE SEQUENCE in which architectural decisions are reached and frozen, then walking it subsystem by subsystem with each subsystem's solution confirmed through its own permission selection — freeze it, then orchestrate fully parallel per-system implementation and e2e authoring, a production-only structural-…[TRUNCATED 1158 chars for corpus]

commands.name: debug-emacs-agent-repl
commands.description: Investigate the agent-repl system across Emacs, daemon, shim, webapp, sidecar, store, state, deployment, logging, and test coverage. Use for current or historical workspace failures, wrong colors or stuck states, missing conversation data, service-health questions, source-versus-running readiness, workspace/session/process correlation, structured-log analysis, SSM or store SQL investigation, coverage questions, missing telemetry, iterative critical-path instrumentation, reload, reproduction, and log-analysis loops, and orchestrated bounce-observe-remediate loops that drive the stack to a healthy steady state. (user)

commands.name: explanation-engine-skill
commands.description: Make changes to the explanation-engine main repository (CEE — CEE is an abbreviation for explanation-engine) via dispatched subagents. Each change is implemented by a subagent in a dedicated workspace — a git worktree of the repo on a fresh branch cut from the default branch — landed as a PR via /create-or-update-pr with self-certified --add-to-merge-queue, and the worktree is cleaned up off disk when the subagent resolves. Use whenever the user asks to make, implement, fix, or land a change in the explanation-engine / CEE main repository through a subagent, whenever the user requests a change to ANY CEE/explanation-engine skill — any skill that lives in the explanation-engine directory — or invokes /explanation-engine-skill. (user)

commands.name: generate-system-graph
commands.description: Build a schema-validated YAML system-graph document from a plain-English system specification: nodes are systems, edges are containment or per-interaction dependencies. Each invocation expands one BFS level of frontier nodes via parallel worker agents (grounded runs peruse the real codebase and cite receipts); /iterate runs it to completion under a depth cap. Use when the user asks to generate, build, grow, or update a system graph, dependency graph, or system model from a specification, or invokes /generate-system-graph. (user)

commands.name: gns-create-project
commands.description: Create Project (user)

commands.name: graphify
commands.description: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools. (user)

commands.name: implement-integrate-resolve
commands.description: implement-integrate-resolve (user)

commands.name: iterate
commands.description: Repeatedly runs a skill (designed for /tests-quality or /tests-coverage), executes each remediation plan, commits the result, and loops until the skill emits ITERATE_SIGNAL: TERMINATE ITERATION SUCCESS/FAILURE or 5 iterations are reached. (user)

commands.name: profile
commands.description: Run a time-boxed Emacs profiling session. Starts the profiler, schedules an automatic stop after N minutes via ScheduleWakeup, then analyzes the resulting profiler-report. Use when the user wants a hands-off profile around a slow editor operation, or invokes /profile. (user)

commands.name: render-system-graph
commands.description: Render a system-graph document (the schema-validated YAML produced by /generate-system-graph) as a Mermaid diagram: containment as nested subgraphs, dependencies as labeled dashed arrows colored by critical-path break impact, node shapes by kind. Validates the document first and refuses to render an invalid graph. Use when the user asks to render, draw, diagram, or visualize a system graph or system-graph document, or invokes /render-system-graph. (user)

commands.name: runtime-eval-code
commands.description: Send elisp to the running Emacs at runtime — evaluate snippets, dump live buffer state, capture *Messages* output, or run a measured snippet inside a profiling session — and receive the result back as a follow-up message. The skill scopes every dispatch to the current workspace so operations like "create a buffer" or "evaluate a file" land in the workspace the agent is running in. Use when you need to inspect or mutate live editor state without rewriting source, when the bug is signaled by 3rd-party output the agent-repl log does not carry, or when pairing with /workspace-profile or /profile to measure exactly one operation. (user)

commands.name: show-chess-game
commands.description: Display an interactive chess board inside the agent-repl GUI response bubble. Use when the user asks to show, render, or display a chess game, position, or live analysis session on a board — from a PGN, a FEN, or a live engine session id. The response carries a one-line marker the GUI renders as the board. (user)

commands.name: tests-coverage
commands.description: Run language-specific coverage tools on unit tests, narrow the report to functions changed in the current context, and produce a remediation plan for uncovered code paths. (user)

commands.name: tests-quality
commands.description: Review test structure and style for changed files against project standards, then produce a remediation plan. Supports context scoping: branch (default), commit, uncommitted. (user)

commands.name: top-level-arch-features
commands.description: Decompose one architectural node at a time into its principal sub-features for a given analysis context. Designed as the inner skill of a BFS decomposition driven by `/iterate` — each pass processes one un-handled member from a sibling list; state is persisted across iterations so the loop resumes where the previous pass left off. (user)

commands.name: top-level-arch-members
commands.description: Decompose one architectural node into its principal sub-members for a given analysis goal, returning a flat JSON array of names (empty array signals no further decomposition is useful). One-shot leaf RPC, never recursive. (user)

commands.name: transfer-claude-context-to-chesscom
commands.description: Transfer the current Claude Code session's full context (its transcript) from the default config dir into a second config dir (default ~/.claude-chesscom) so the same session can be resumed, in the same workspace/cwd, under the new config dir. Use when the user wants to restart this session under a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR without losing history, or invokes /transfer-claude-context-to-chesscom. (user)

commands.name: workspace-close
commands.description: Close an existing editor workspace without merging it. Use when the user wants to dispatch a close for one or more named workspaces (kill its Claude session, buffers, and Doom perspective) without cherry-picking commits anywhere, asks to "/workspace-close", or wants to discard a workspace's editor state while leaving the git worktree on disk untouched. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: gns-cowork:gns-bootstrap

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat t…[TRUNCATED 735 chars for corpus]

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: statusline-setup
agents.description: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting.

agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: statusline-setup
agents.description: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting.
